text: Zip lets you loop over two or more lists at the same time, in parallel, pairing up their items.
Each turn of the loop, you get one name and the matching age, lined up by position.
So the two separate lists read as if they were one list of pairs.
[chuckle] If the lists are different lengths, zip simply stops at the shortest one, no error.
So pairing a four-item list with a two-item list gives you just two pairs.
[sniff] zip pairs beautifully with dict, stitching two lists into a dictionary of keys and values.
And there's a reverse trick — zip with a star unzips a list of pairs back into separate sequences.
The numbers land in one tuple, the letters in another, cleanly separated.
[groan] zip is the tool whenever your data lives in several parallel lists that belong together.
